topics.label: Introduction and lecture learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecturer, the course context, and the learning objectives for the lecture on cancer causation.

topics.label: Concepts of cancer etiology, mutation sources, and epidemiological variation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the foundational framework of cancer causation by evaluating the relative contributions of intrinsic biological errors, inherited genetic predispositions, and environmental exposures across global populations.

topics.label: Infectious pathogens in carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how viral and bacterial pathogens contribute to oncogenesis, highlighting Burkitt lymphoma and other infection-driven malignancies as primary models.

topics.label: Chemical and physical mutagens and mechanisms of DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the molecular mechanisms by which radiation, dietary compounds, and environmental chemicals undergo metabolic activation to induce DNA adducts and mutations.

topics.label: Tumor promotion, non-mutagenic mechanisms, and host susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how non-mutagenic factors like chronic inflammation, promoter signalling pathways, and tissue proliferation states drive neoplastic outgrowth from initiated cells.

topics.label: Methods for identifying carcinogens and assessing cancer risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the sequencing, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro approaches used to determine the carcinogenicity of exposures and evaluate real-world risks.

topics.label: Lecture summary and conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture with a final summary of environmental cancer risks, detection challenges, and everyday risk-benefit considerations.
